$comment: SAF CLI accepts a count bound in two shapes: an object ({min, max}) and a bare scalar. Measured in mitre/saf src/commands/validate/threshold.ts (pinned 705d3f26), which guards the scalar path with `typeof !== 'object'` and then asserts `count !== N` — so a scalar means EXACTLY N, not a minimum. Both languages read this table so they cannot disagree about that. Go reaches it through ThresholdBound's YAML decoding; TypeScript does no YAML decoding of its own, so it reaches the same rule through normalizeThresholdConfig, which a consumer calls on whatever it parsed. cases[].bound is the value as written in a spec; want is the ThresholdBound it must mean.

cases.name: a scalar is an exact bound, not a minimum
zero is a bound, not an absence
an object with only min keeps max unset
an object with only max keeps min unset
an object carrying both is unchanged
an object carrying controls is unchanged
